title: POC scoping: data handling & success criteria - NovusCare
summary: POC scoping focused on data handling requirements for a 4-week pilot: redaction/logging controls, retention policy, prompt storage limits, and success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost). Agreement to run Redwood hosted POC with private VPC options if needed; SE to run baseline benchmarks; security team to review SOC2 docs and KMS integration.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-21 16:00 PDT | Duration ~48m | Attendees: Alex Morgan, Priya Shah (Redwood) — Anya Patel, Tom Reynolds, Lisa Gomez (NovusCare)

[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick rollcall?
[00:08] Dr. Anya Patel: hi Alex, Anya here, Tom and Lisa are on as well.
[00:11] Tom Reynolds: hey all.
[00:12] Lisa Gomez: hi.
[00:15] Alex Morgan: great, the goal today is to scope data handling for the POC — what we need to prove, what data flows look like, and timeline. Priya from our SE team will cover benchmarks.
[00:28] Priya Shah: yep, I have a short benchmark plan and questions about PII, retention, and whether you want prompt storage.
[00:35] Lisa Gomez: security first — we need to know if any customer PII will be persisted, if logs contain prompt text, and how long stuff is retained. also KMS for keys, and SOC2 artifacts.
[00:47] Alex Morgan: totally, we usually do options: (1) no prompt retention — ephemeral only; (2) prompt retention with redaction; (3) VPC/private deployment so logs never leave customer network. which do you prefer for the POC?
[01:02] Dr. Anya Patel: for the pilot we'd like redaction + short retention for debugging: retention window of 7 days max. we also need redaction of PHI — names, MRNs, DOBs — and a guarantee prompts won't be used for model training.
[01:20] Priya Shah: Redwood supports redact-on-ingest and we can configure per-route retention settings; training use is disabled for customer data and we'll include that in the contract. redaction isn't perfect — sometimes tokenization splits names — we'll show you how detection works in the test.
[01:37] Tom Reynolds: workload sizing — expected traffic for the POC is roughly 5k requests/day, avg 600 tokens per request, peak concurrency ~30. does that align with your benchmarking?
[01:50] Priya Shah: yes, we can run 5k/day profile. for hosted we run continuous batching; p95 latency target you care about?
[01:58] Dr. Anya Patel: p50 under 200ms, p95 under 1.2s for short responses (<=1024 tokens). if we hit worse latency, we need escalation.
[02:11] Priya Shah: noted. in benchmarks we'll report p50/p95/p99, throughput (req/s), GPU util, and token cost. we'll also run a KV cache prefix test to see cost savings for repeated prompts.
[02:27] Lisa Gomez: about logs: can we mask the prompt text in logs and still keep metadata like request id, route, model? we need to keep traceability for debugging but not PII.
[02:38] Alex Morgan: yes, we can store a hashed prompt fingerprint and remove the raw prompt; metadata preserved. or we can store redacted prompt where PHI replaced with [REDACTED]. both are common.
[02:50] Tom Reynolds: what's your retention config UI look like? can we set retention per-project route?
[02:55] Priya Shah: yes per-route retention; for the POC we'll set 7 days for prompts and 90 days for non-PII metrics by default, configurable.
[03:06] Dr. Anya Patel: compliance: we need SOC2 and ISO docs, plus an explanation of key handling — we prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS.
[03:16] Alex Morgan: we support KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can enable a bring-your-own-key flow for enterprise — will share security pack.
[03:25] Lisa Gomez: any differences in redaction capabilities between hosted and private?
[03:29] Priya Shah: functionally similar; private/VPC gives you more control over log egress and optional on-prem pipelines. redaction models run in the same runtime but you can choose to run them inside your VPC in Private deployment.
[03:44] Tom Reynolds: benchmarks & timeline — what's realistic for a 4-week POC?
[03:48] Priya Shah: week 0: kick off + access; week 1: baseline benchmarks (5k/day profile) + redaction tests; week 2: integration with your dev stack + more targeted workload; week 3: end-to-end validation and evaluation against success criteria; week 4: final report and handoff. we can compress if both sides prioritize.
[04:06] Dr. Anya Patel: success criteria: (1) redaction reliability > 95% on sample PHI set; (2) latency targets met p95 <1.2s; (3) cost per 1k tokens below our threshold — we'll share numbers; (4) no data used for training and retention enforced.
[04:27] Alex Morgan: yep, we'll measure with the eval harness. Priya will run the benchmark and provide CSV + dashboards.
[04:35] Lisa Gomez: prompt storage concern: we need a policy for prompt history used for context windows — some of our prompts contain patient identifiers in free text. do you recommend client-side redaction before sending?
[04:47] Priya Shah: if possible client-side redaction is best — that gives you maximum control. otherwise we recommend passing a sanitized prompt and retaining only redacted or hashed prompt server-side. we can provide a small SDK helper to do deterministic masking for common PHI patterns.
[05:05] Tom Reynolds: any limitations on snapshotting logs for audits? we may need full audit logs for 1 year for a subset of events.
[05:12] Lisa Gomez: correct, audit logs for admin actions for 12 months.
[05:15] Alex Morgan: audit logs (admin actions) can be exported to your S3 or to Splunk; for PII-containing payloads we recommend shorter retention. we'll note that in the security doc.
[05:27] Priya Shah: one more technical: if you want to test KV cache and batching effects on cost, we'll run a baseline with and without caching. that usually shows a 20-40% token cost reduction for conversational workloads.
[05:41] Dr. Anya Patel: good. for the pilot, can Redwood guarantee that model updates won't change outputs mid-POC? we need deterministic behavior.
[05:50] Alex Morgan: you can pin model versions for the POC; automatic updates are off unless you opt-in. we'll deploy the same version across hosts for consistency.
[05:59] Tom Reynolds: ok logistics — what access do you need?
[06:02] Priya Shah: API key (scoped), sample dataset (anonymized but with PHI markers), and a list of routes you want to exercise. for KMS we need key ARN if using CMK.
[06:16] Lisa Gomez: we'll provide Anonymized dataset plus a PHI sample set. we'll also open a support ticket for SOC2 docs.
[06:22] Alex Morgan: perfect. quick recap before we close.
[06:25] Alex Morgan: recap: run 5k/day benchmark, redaction tests, retention set to 7 days for prompts, provide SOC2 & KMS options, timeline roughly 4 weeks, success criteria as stated.
[06:36] Dr. Anya Patel: sounds good.
[06:38] Tom Reynolds: yep.
[06:39] Lisa Gomez: thank you.
[06:40] Alex Morgan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with security pack and benchmark plan.

Note: transcription contains occasional errors and speaker overlaps — e.g., 'redact-on-ingest' might appear as 'redact on gist' in auto-transcript.
